question: What fish evidence does the 2011 Bolinao mangrove-management study report, and what remains unresolved before it could support public species or waterbody records?

method.summary: Reviewed the Silliman Journal article landing page, publisher-hosted full-text PDF methods and fish/invertebrate section, Vol. 52 No. 2 issue record, and journal copyright policy. No article table, map, photograph, raw dataset, or local PDF snapshot was retained.
method.bibliographicDateFinding: The issue listing and printed PDF identify Silliman Journal Vol. 52 No. 2 (2011), July–December 2011. The migrated article page displays Published 2022-10-07; this page date is recorded separately from the issue date.
method.surveyFinding: The paper says fish and invertebrates were sampled in November–December 2009 in the mangrove-management areas of Arnedo, Balingasay, Binabalian, and Victory, Bolinao. It describes three fish-sampling stations and ten 10 m by 5 m quadrats per station in a stated 1,500 m² per barangay. Fish and invertebrates were assessed using a 10 m by 1 m gill net set for two hours on a falling tide and cover pots used at low tide; photographs were taken to aid identification. The text reviewed names the barangays but supplies no machine-readable station coordinates or datum and no voucher/accession identifiers.
method.reportedCounts: The abstract and results report 18 fish-and-invertebrate taxa overall, described in the body as four fish and 14 invertebrate species. Table 6 gives site-level richness values of 14, 17, 9, and 11 for Arnedo, Balingasay, Binabalian, and Victory respectively; these site totals overlap and are not additive. The three high-importance labels emphasized in the abstract are classified as invertebrates in the article's fish/invertebrate section, not as fish.
method.habitatAndWaterQualityLimit: The source is about coastal mangrove-management areas, not an inland river or lake survey. Its water-quality section reports 35 ppt salinity at four stations, but those are water-parameter stations and must not be mistaken for the three fish-sampling stations per barangay or used to infer a precise waterbody boundary.
method.rightsFinding: The Silliman Journal policy states published-article copyright is held by the journal and individual authors and describes permission requirements for reuse. No Creative Commons or item-specific permission for a derived species dataset was verified. No table, figure, photo, full article text, or raw dataset was retained; public-app reuse is not approved.

publication.title: Assessment of Mangrove Management Areas in Four Coastal Barangays of Bolinao, Pangasinan, Philippines
publication.citation: Paz-Alberto, A. M., & Teñoso, A. R. D. (2011). Assessment of Mangrove Management Areas in Four Coastal Barangays of Bolinao, Pangasinan, Philippines. Silliman Journal, 52(2).
publication.accessStatus: Publisher landing page, issue record, full-text PDF methods/results, and journal copyright policy reviewed online on 2026-11-19.
publication.license: No open license or item-specific data-reuse grant verified. The journal copyright policy states published-article copyright is held by the journal and individual authors.

internalConsistency.issue: The article abstract reports 24 mangrove species, while its results section says 23; this is a mangrove-plant count discrepancy and does not change the reported fish/invertebrate count.
internalConsistency.disposition: Keep the source's mangrove totals flagged as inconsistent; this review does not use them as fish or waterbody evidence.

internalConsistency.issue: The fish/invertebrate section reports four fish and 14 invertebrates overall, while Table 6 reports separate site richness values of 14, 17, 9, and 11.
internalConsistency.disposition: Treat the latter as overlapping per-site richness, not additive totals; no raw occurrence matrix was extracted or independently recalculated.

internalConsistency.issue: The prose spells the goby label Periopthalmus barbarous while Table 3 spells it Periopthalmus barbarus.
internalConsistency.disposition: Preserve both source strings and their locations for a separate taxonomic crosscheck; do not silently normalize or assert an organism identity.

internalConsistency.issue: The article page displays Published 2022-10-07 although its issue and printed PDF identify Vol. 52 No. 2 (2011).
internalConsistency.disposition: Record the original issue period and migrated-page date separately.

interpretation: This is a historical source lead for coastal mangrove habitat in four named Bolinao barangays; it is not a complete Bolinao, Pangasinan, or Region I fish checklist and does not establish current presence or catch probability.

The fish study used capture gear at named barangay-scale mangrove areas. It does not provide machine-readable sampling points, voucher/accession identifiers, or a precise named-waterbody assignment in the reviewed text. Do not infer a reach, mangrove polygon, or navigation geometry from the article figure.

The paper's late-2009 mangrove sampling is distinct in habitat and method from the same authors' late-2009 MPA snorkeling visual census in the same four barangays. Keep the two evidence contexts separate and do not combine their counts or treat them as independent regional baselines without author/source clarification.
The reported 35 ppt values are from the water-quality subsection and do not resolve station coordinates or justify a site-level brackish classification.
The article's three highlighted high-importance labels are invertebrates in its results section. Preserve that distinction; they are not fish recommendations.

The journal copyright policy was reviewed, but no item-specific license or permission was established. No taxa table, map, photo, raw data, occurrence row, species assertion, geometry, or public-app content was added. Region I and Luzon remain incomplete.

decision.reason: The paper provides a historical mangrove fish/invertebrate survey claim but has no machine-readable station coordinates or reviewed voucher links, includes source-name variants, and has no verified item-specific data-reuse license.

nextAction: Run a bounded authority crosscheck on the four fish strings while preserving the article spellings and treating all results as name candidates only; then continue the Region I source sweep across estuaries, rivers, lakes, wetlands, and marine waters.
